| 3 | `bse_code_mapping.json` present in source but omitted from `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` | `bootstrap.py::restore_omitted_package_data` (SHA-256 verified) | `OMITTED_PACKAGE_DATA` |
| 4 | Global tip watermark made every `derive adj_factors` run incremental (median 1 row/symbol) | cleared derived watermark, then drained the bounded 500-symbol realignment backlog | — |
| 5 | CDR `689009.SH` is the only non-exact symbol; `derive/adj_factors.py:441` filters to `stock`/`etf` | kept **visible in the denominator**, excluded from numerator; **0 gate flips** | `CDR_FACTOR_SUPPORT_DEFERRED` |
| 6 | BSE board is **tip-only** (347 rows today, 0 for past dates, `complete=True`) | sidecar tip-bridge with honest provenance; never back-stamped | `BJ_TIP_SNAPSHOT_PIT_SEMANTICS_V1` |
| 7 | `TDX_EXCHANGES = {"SH","SZ"}` excluded BJ, so every BJ symbol fell to the Sina tip lane | sidecar widens the set to include `BJ` | `BEIJING_AWARE_QUOTE_PARTITION_V1` |

### 2.1 The BJ fix in full (this is the one that unblocked Beijing)

`domain/symbols.py:91` declares `TDX_EXCHANGES = frozenset({"SH", "SZ"})`, so
`is_tdx_servable("920000.BJ")` is `False` and `steps/bars.py:853` pushes every BJ symbol to the Sina
fallback lane. The TDX protocol **does** serve Beijing (measured: **358 rows**, full OHLCV+amount, for
`920000.BJ` and `920001.BJ`), and the pin's own `_fetch_bj_history_via_tdx` says so. The sidecar adds
`"BJ"` to the set at runtime; the fetcher is untouched.

Measured effect: BJ went **347 tip rows → 94,972 rows** (median **358**/symbol,
`2025-04-10 → 2026-09-24`), `sina` stayed at exactly 347 (tip only), and **BJ exact ratio = 1.000000**.
